text:
The finite W-D2E experiment is useful as a bounded equality fixture. It does not close normative W-D2. Equality here means field 26 matches SHA-256 of a caller-supplied record. Semantic correctness is a separate property, and the packet contains a case where equality holds while Core rejects.

## Verdicts

| Question | Verdict | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Useful finite W-D2E experiment | **Accept, bounded.** Canonical finite encoder, six financially coherent positive images, hostile preimage separation, field-26 equality, and an explicit equality-versus-Core split. | Moderate-high. Layout and financial traces were checked on the embedded bytes. SHA-256 was not recomputed. Node was not re-run. |
| Normative W-D2 closure | **Reject. Open.** | High. |
| Wallet, signature, proof, native, or ledger acceptance | **Not established.** No acceptance claim is available from this packet. | High. |

This is one reviewer seat (Grok). GPT-6.1 Sol was requested and was not run. Delegation was forbidden by the review charter, so that seat is an abstention, not a second verdict.

Internal dissent, preserved: a stricter reading would grade the finite experiment **incomplete** rather than accept-bounded. Field 26 is checked against an out-of-band `prepared` object. The signed operation, caps, nonce, signer, and preHead are not inputs to the comparison. On that reading the packet shows byte equality of a supplied image, and it has not yet shown that the signed terms commit those effects. The primary verdict stays accept-bounded because the specification scopes that weaker claim and the six positive transitions are financially right.

## Evidence grades

**Observed in the embedded sources and hex.** Effect-codec compare is hash equality after `decodeAuthorization`. Extra root keys `authorizationDigest`, `effectCommitment`, and `signature` fail `SHAPE` because the own-key set is exact. Header is 22 bytes, `moriarty-s0-effects/1` plus NUL. Round `100` is eight big-endian bytes. Transfer-fee debit amount is the 16-byte value `0x0b`; changed-debit is the same image with `0x0c`. Zero-fee effect count is 5 and balance count is 3. Dropping one credit changes length 583 to 560 (23 bytes, one credit line). Dropping one balance row changes 583 to 548 (35 bytes). Adding one replay-history entry changes 583 to 621 (38 bytes). Repay images are 688 bytes; the +105 from the 583-byte transfer image is one credit replaced by `SetObligation` (+30), one fewer balance row (−35), and one obligation row (+110). Settled `SetObligation` carries status byte `0x02`. Near-bound bytes contain nominal `0x7f…fe` / `0x7f…ff` and u128 `0xff…fe` / `0xff…ff` separately. Root-head bytes put `0xbb` in the root preHead and leave AdvanceHead’s predecessor as `0x55`. Successor-line bytes leave the root successor as `0xaa` and put `0xbb` on the AdvanceHead successor. Premise failure is code `LITERAL` and has no frozen digest. Test source arithmetic is 6×2 positive tests + 19 hostile + 33 schema + 3 extras = 67. TAP text says `1..67`, `# pass 67`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0`.

**Packet claims, internally consistent, not re-executed here.** Freeze receipt at `2026-09-30T07:45:25.599254+00:00` with `codecExisted: false`. Same-author Python construction. Captured `node --test` green run on Node v24.21.0. Red log is a startup `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, which the result text already calls a load failure rather than a semantic red. The first green run had 64 checks; three schema checks were added later. Hash strings for the same paths agree across the manifest, freeze receipt, `results.json`, and `artifact-sha256.json`. Bin lengths in the manifest match the frozen vector lengths. Each bin’s recorded SHA-256 equals that vector’s commitment, which is the claimed relationship for “file = preimage”. Those digests were not recomputed in this review.

**Manual trace of the embedded Core/5 source against the six fixtures.** `prepareMil4S0` recomputes the same ordered effects and the same candidate post. Footprint and consumption in `prepared` also match that transition. The test harness itself checks effects, candidate post, and the four premise names. It does not assert footprint or consumption against Core.

## Circularity

The effect preimage has no authorization digest, effect commitment, signature, or proof field. A well-shaped record is a function of schema version, Core/5 literal, domain, asset, scale, operation kind, round, preHead, successor, ordered lines, footprint, consumption, and the premise gate. Field 26 is wire tag 26 (`effectCommitment`, the 26th tagged authorization field). The authorization digest is defined over authorization bytes that include that field. That dependency is acyclic.

The schema exclusion is real for own properties on the effect object. It does not constrain how a producer chooses `successor`. In the fixtures the successor is the constant `aa` repeated, so those six images are not digest-derived. The codec will commit any 32-byte lowercase hex successor it is given. Independence of the head remains a producer premise, as the specification says.

Replacing the effect bytes and field 26 together is still equality. `compareEffectCommitment` returns `CommitmentEqualUnqualified` whenever the decoded field equals SHA-256 of the supplied record. The changed-debit recommitment test encodes that case, and the source does that even if the captured TAP is set aside.

## Canonicality

Positional big-endian layout, schema key order, preserved array order, lowercase hex, and canonical decimal strings are implemented in both the Python oracle and the JS encoder. Property-order reversal is specified to keep the same bytes. Line order and balance-row order are specified to change the bytes. The split-head hex shows disagreements are committed rather than normalized. That part of the candidate is doing the job the specification describes.

Four canonicality limits stay inside the candidate:

- `requiredPremises` and the Core/5 string are checked, then replaced by the single bytes `0x0f` and `0x05`. A later encoder can change the hardcoded string list and still emit `0x0f`. Reordered premises never become an alternate commitment; they die as `LITERAL`.
- There is no effect decoder and no inverse test. Encoder agreement on a finite set leaves uniqueness of decoding untested.
- Effect-codec and wire identifiers allow a leading digit, `:`, and `/`. Core/5 identifiers are a leading letter and `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` only. The six fixtures use single letters, inside the intersection. The codec can commit account names Core/5 will not stage.
- Replay nonces on this wire are exactly 64 lowercase hex bytes. Core’s `opaque` nonce is wider. These fixtures agree. The effect image cannot represent every Core-legal replay key.
- An extra inherited enumerable property, with the own-key set already exact, is dropped rather than rejected. An inherited required field is rejected. The specification’s word “reject” covers the second case. The committed image still excludes inherited data.
- Replay component failures are rethrown as `REPLAY`, so a too-long id inside a replay key does not surface as `LENGTH`.

Python `reference_bytes` is an encoder for already-well-formed literals. Its unknown-kind branch treats the line as AdvanceHead. It does not enforce the 4096-byte cap or the nominal cap. JS is the rejecting encoder. Agreement on the frozen vectors is transcription agreement with one specification, by one author, not a second design.

## What the six positive images commit

Traced from the literals through embedded Core arithmetic, and checked against the footprint fields. Principal + accrued = outstanding holds in every repay image. Settled appears only when outstanding is 0.

| Case | Transition | Length | Commitment (packet) |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| transfer-fee | Debit 11, credit R 10, credit F 1. Owner 100→89, R 0→10, F 0→1. Allowance 11/0→0/11. | 583 | `bc633665…cb7c0e` |
| transfer-zero-fee | Debit 10, credit R 10, no fee line. F remains 4→4 and is still in the footprint. Allowance 20/3→10/13. | 560 | `ed5b4bff…a5aa6d` |
| repay-30 | Accrual-first 30 on 1000+10. Accrued 10 then principal 20. Result 980+0, outstanding 980. Cash 100→70 and 0→30. | 688 | `e8b64f93…c04888` |
| repay-accrued-only | Payment 5 from accrued. Principal stays 1000. Accrued 10→5. Outstanding 1010→1005. | 688 | `90b113d7…2898fa` |
| repay-settled | Payment 1010 clears 1000+10. Outstanding 0, status byte `0x02`. | 688 | `006f01a1…3baa90` |
| repay-near-bound | Payment 1 clears accrued 1. Principal stays 2^127−2. Creditor balance and allowance spent land on 2^128−1. Outstanding before is 2^127−1. | 688 | `f0889508…226d43` |

Each positive image also moves work 2/7→1/8, appends one composite replay key, and advances `55…` to `aa…`. Those consumption fields are in the frozen tail hex. Core returns `PreparedUnqualified` for each of the six when the submitted lines are these lines. That status is an unqualified local preparation. It is not ledger admission.

`transfer-fee` sits on the effect cap of 6, so the appended-line hostile is taken from the five-line zero-fee image and stays encodable. Reject-at-7 is a separate `LENGTH` control. That cap boundary is intentional and coherent.

The Python gross for the fee case is the literal `'11'`, selected by case name, rather than a general amount-plus-fee computation. It matches Core for this fee of 1. It is a generator footgun for any later nonzero fee.

## Binding

The consumer binds one thing: canonical bytes of the object passed as `prepared`, under SHA-256, to decoded field 26. It does not read `authorization.operation`, `grossCap`, `feeCap`, `netFloor`, `nonce`, `signer`, `preHead`, or `scale`.

A prepared debit of 12, with the original transfer operation still saying amount 10 and fee 1, compares equal once field 26 is replaced with `a4138995…2ba173`. Embedded Core then returns `Rejected` / `S0_EFFECT_MISMATCH` and publishes no post-state. That split is the load-bearing result of the experiment.

The same function will commit a non-conserving image. Changed-debit is debit 12 against credits 10+1, a balance delta of 11, and an allowance of 11. Those disagreements stay in the bytes. Nothing in the codec repairs them.

Signed caps are covered by the authorization digest only if some other component verifies the signature over those authorization bytes. This consumer does not. Changing field 26 changes `authorizationDigest` in the test. That shows the digest input includes field 26. It does not verify a signature.

## Python, JS, and Core/5

`reference-vectors.py` imports `struct`, `hashlib`, `json`, `copy`, and `pathlib` only. Expected financial numbers are literals. The post-state work step is the constant 2/7→1/8, not a call into Core.

The freeze receipt covers `SPEC.md`, `PLAN.md`, `reference-vectors.py`, and `fixtures.json`. It does not cover `codec.test.mjs`. Hash agreement across packet artifacts supports “these texts are the texts whose hashes were recorded”. It does not independently witness wall-clock order. The red log shows that some test file imported `codec.mjs` before that module resolved. It does not show that all 67 assertions already existed. The result text is candid that three checks were added after the first green run.

Core/5 comparison is a real recomputation for effects and candidate post on these six literals. It is not cross-layer correspondence. Scale and operation kind live in the effect image and in the wire authorization; Core’s repay intent has no allocation field and always applies accrual-first arithmetic. The wire codec forces the literal `AccrualFirst`. The effect image commits the resulting numbers, not the policy name.

## Sixty-seven tests and hostile strength

The 67-count is structurally real in `codec.test.mjs`, and the embedded TAP names the same 67 subtests with zero failures and zero skips. Treat that as captured packet evidence. This review did not launch Node.

The eighteen encodable hostiles are a strong differential set for this finite schema: amount, dropped line, appended line, full line reversal, recipient, allowance amount, work counter, omitted balance row, balance value, allowance pre-state, obligation debtor, principal line versus footprint, replay nonce, replay history, replay domain, root head, successor line, and balance-row order. Their frozen commitment prefixes are pairwise distinct, and several preimage edits were checked directly in the hex.

Hostile strength stops at the preimage. The suite does not contain a second allowance, a second obligation, a zero debit, an unknown obligation status, or a harness assertion that footprint equals Core’s post. The test named “unknown status” mutates `operationKind` to `netted` and expects `VARIANT`. That assertion matches the shared variant branch. It does not exercise obligation status.

The premise-order case correctly fails closed. It does not show that premise text is inside the hash.

## Closure conditions still open

The packet’s own limits match the code. Still open, and untouched by an equality pass: producer selection of the head, signature verification, binding field 26 to the signed operation, footprint completeness, state and head authentication, replay consumption, atomic compare-and-consume, an effect decoder, a circuit or proof, Source/6 correspondence, native verification, wallet behavior, and ledger settlement. The caps (4096 bytes, 6 effects, 3 balances, 1 allowance, 1 obligation, 16 replay entries) are experimental bounds. SHA-256 collision resistance is assumed, not demonstrated.

These bytes are a finite candidate image. They are not a normative W-D2 selection.
